page: Amazon Web Services g5g.8xlarge is an ARM64-based server powered by 32 dedicated AWS Neoverse-N1 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance includes a single NVIDIA T4G GPU from the Turing family with 16 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled, and network connectivity is rated at a 12 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,574.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,551.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 952.0 and weak single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached small blocks at 1,892.97 GB/sec, but drops to 161.7 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, with Passmark memory scores falling into the lower tier. For LLM inference, the server achieves an average prompt processing speed of 31.98 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model, though text generation on a small 135M model is poor at 42.38 tokens/sec.

Given its ARM64 architecture and integrated NVIDIA T4G GPU, this server offers a specialized hardware profile designed for cost-efficient graphics and machine learning workloads. The dedicated Neoverse-N1 cores and GPU acceleration make it suitable for Android game streaming, ray tracing, image processing, and medium-scale LLM inference. However, the lack of local storage and lower single-core performance are notable tradeoffs for workloads requiring high sequential disk access or single-threaded execution.
